From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@helioshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95/p99 regressions — triage notes

Triage update (initial):
- Observed behavior: host-side queue depth increased sharply at ~08:47; the batching window expanded from median 18ms -> 460ms due to a handful of long-running requests (tail requests) creating backpressure. This allowed batches to accumulate and increased p95/p99 dramatically.
- Root cause hypothesis: a small percentage (~0.6%) of Helios requests have unusually large context and tokenization patterns that produce much larger compute time; these long requests landed on the same worker shard and increased its processing time, enlarging local batching windows.
- Correlated signals: KV cache hit rates dropped for Helios prefix (suggests wider variance of prefixes), one inference worker reported repeated CUDA kernel recompile warnings at 08:45 which increased processing times for Llama-variant kernels.

Immediate mitigations we can try (order of execution):
1) Temporarily reduce max_batch_delay_ms for Helios route to 50ms (current 300ms) to limit batch accumulation and bound tail amplification.
2) Enable priority routing for Helios traffic (move to warm hot path) to isolate from public bursts.
3) Spin a small burst pool (2x ephemeral GPUs) and funnel Helios traffic there for the next 2 hours.
4) If mitigation insufficient, fallback Helios to a slightly lower-cost model variant with shorter per-token kernels for the next 30m to reduce compute tail.

I can apply 1–3 right away; applying 4 requires Marissa’s sign-off for an emergency downgrade and comms.

Logs attached: small trace excerpts and the slot-by-slot batch histogram.

—Dylan (SRE)

- Impact window: 08:47–10:05 PDT (p95 peaked at 2.3s, p99 >10s, ~1.8% 5xx)

- Actions taken: reduced max_batch_delay_ms for the Helios route, spun up a 2-node burst pool and enabled priority routing, allowed emergency fallback to a faster model variant.
- Ask: approve one-time credit up to 10% of March hosted usage for Helios (estimate $6.5k) and priority allocation of Dedicated capacity evaluation (customer has asked about Dedicated to avoid noisy neighbors).
